### Observed differences

- **Branching after A02 moved toward the forward path.** Earlier, about 90 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions went on to A04 and about 9–10 in 100 returned to A01; in the later window about 94 in 100 go to A04 and only about 5–6 in 100 return to A01 — the return was taken in roughly 19 of 200 traces earlier versus about 11 later. [DIR002, LAG007]
- **Branching after A04 moved toward the return.** Earlier, about 96–97 in 100 of A04's outgoing transitions went to A03 and about 3–4 in 100 returned to A01; later about 93–94 go to A03 and about 6–7 return to A01 — roughly 7 versus 13 traces out of 200. [DIR004, LAG014]
- **Placement of the returns shifted accordingly.** Among the roughly 30 versus 25 traces where A02 is followed by A01 within five steps, returns at the very next event fell from about 63 to 44 in 100 while returns one event later rose from about 23 to 52 in 100; among the roughly 11 versus 14 traces where A04 is followed by A01, next-event returns rose from about 64 to 93 in 100. [LAG005, LAG013]
- **A01's own forward skips redistributed.** Direct skips from A01 to A04 fell from about 9.5 to 5.5 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, skips to A03 rose from about 3.5 to 6.5 in 100, and the rare direct edge to A06 (about 1–2 in 100, a few traces) was not observed in the later window; the pair-lag profiles match (A01→A04 at the next event 10→6 in 100; A01→A03 at the next event about 3.6→6.5 in 100). [DIR001, LAG001, LAG002]
- **No repositioning or reordering.** Event positions of all six activities are essentially unchanged (medians identical, mean shifts of at most about 0.01 position units), and order relations barely moved — A01 precedes A02 in 85 versus 87.5 in 100 traces, and A05/A06 keep no fixed order (about 52/48 in both windows). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]

### Inference

Support level: Weak hypothesis

The evidence suggests, as a possibility, that the rework returns into A01 shifted from the loop after A02 to the loop after A04. In the earlier window, cases returning to A01 did so mostly directly after A02 (about 9–10 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions, roughly 19 of 200 traces) and rarely after A04 (about 3–4 in 100, roughly 7 traces); in the later window the A02 return fell to roughly half (about 5–6 in 100, roughly 11 traces) while the A04 return roughly doubled (about 6–7 in 100, roughly 13 traces), with the forward edges A02→A04 and A04→A03 absorbing exactly the difference. Supporting signs: the share changes are measured directly on the outgoing transitions with full support in both windows, they are mirrored by the pair-lag distributions (returns after A04 now almost always at the next event; residual returns after A02 typically one event later), order relations move only trivially, and all involved activities occur in essentially every trace in both windows — consistent with existing branches being taken with different frequencies rather than any structural replacement. What is missing: the return edges are rare (about 3–15 in 100 of traces), so the shifts rest on roughly 7–19 versus 11–19 observations, the two most distinctive lag shifts rest on only about 11–14 and 25–30 traces, and no screening baseline is provided to compare the number of qualifying items against a chance expectation. [DIR002, DIR004, LAG005, LAG007, LAG013, LAG014, REL001, REL003]

Other differences: A01's own outgoing branch redistributed — less often directly to A04, more often directly to A03, with the rare direct edge to A06 unobserved later — and the very rare return from A03 to A01 (about 2 in 100 traces earlier, a single case later) shows no reliable change. [DIR001, LAG001, LAG002, DIR003, LAG010]

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is ordinary sampling variability in an unchanged process: the effects are small (about 3–4 share points in 100), the rare return edges yield few observations, and several indicators describe the same transitions rather than independent confirmations. [DIR002, DIR004, LAG005, LAG013]
